message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive engineering and logistical challenge.  The tower is 324 m (1,063 ft) tall, weighs about 10,100 t, and is made of thousands of individual iron plates.  A full repaint would involve:

| Task | Rough effort | Typical crew size | Estimated time |
|------|--------------|-------------------|----------------|
| **Site preparation & scaffolding** | Build and secure temporary platforms, install safety nets, set up cranes | 50–70 workers | 1–2 months |
| **Surface cleaning & rust removal** | Power‑wash, sandblast, remove old paint & rust | 30–40 workers | 1–2 months |
| **Primer & base coat** | Apply primer, first coat of paint | 30–40 workers | 1–2 months |
| **Top‑coat layers** | Apply multiple layers of protective paint | 30–40 workers | 1–2 months |
| **Detail work & finishing** | Paint railings, decorative elements, touch‑ups | 20–30 workers | 1–2 months |

Adding up the phases, a dedicated crew working full‑time would need roughly **12–18 months** to complete a full repaint.  In practice, the French Ministry of Culture and the Eiffel Tower’s management usually schedule the work in stages over several years, often taking **2–3 years** to finish the entire project while keeping the tower open to visitors.

If you’re asking whether it’s feasible to paint the whole tower in a single continuous effort, the answer is no – the tower is open to the public, and the work is staged to minimize disruption.  So, while a single crew could theoretically finish in about a year and a half, the actual project is spread out over a few years.
